fields.rt-blog-html:
In the fast-food sector, improving team productivity is essential to satisfying your customers, while maintaining the profitability of your outlet. Between task optimization, digitalization and human resources management, every detail counts in delivering optimal service. Discover our practical tips for improving your team's performance: a win-win approach to boosting your business and building customer loyalty every day!

‍

Evaluating restaurant productivity: key indicators

To better understand and improve your restaurant's profitability, it's essential to accurately measure your team's productivity. Focus on 3 key indicators that provide a complete picture of a restaurant's productivity:

Customer satisfaction

It depends directly on the performance of the team. Less waiting time and a quality welcome create a loyal clientele, who will return often and recommend the restaurant to others. Indicators such as footfall and fill rate are revealing.

The figures

KPIs concerning your restaurant's profitability (break-even point, sales, net margin, etc.) are essential for tracking the concrete results of productivity and optimization efforts. They enable you to pinpoint excessive costs or moments of underperformance, andadjust strategies according to the data collected.

Brand image

Great service doesn't go unnoticed. A productive team and smooth service reinforce your brand image and attract new customers. Increased footfall, good customer reviews... All this gives you a concrete idea of the image of your restaurant in the minds of your customers. 

👉 Further information: Key performance indicators for the foodservice industry

‍

9 concrete actions to boost your teams' productivity

1. Optimize order taking to save time

Order-taking is one of the key steps to greater efficiency. Adopting order terminals or QR codes for order-taking and payment reduces errors andspeeds up service, while freeing up time for your employees. This automation reduces repetitive interactions and allows staff to concentrate on more qualitative tasks.

2. Structure tasks for smoother workflows

Work organization is essential to productivity. Define roles and optimize workspaces to avoid unnecessary movement. In the kitchen, for example, a well thought-out layout can significantly improve workflow. Rotating tasks and distributing them appropriately also helps to keep employees motivated, while ensuring maximum efficiency!

3. Integrate digital tools to simplify management

Digitalization brings concrete solutions to restaurateurs. Centralized management software can simplify team planning, inventory tracking and sales analysis. With an integrated cash register system, performance monitoring and order management become much smoother, limiting errors and optimizing working time. Digital tools help streamline every stage of your business, saving time and boosting productivity.

4. Monitor your performance indicators regularly

Keeping track of your performance indicators enables you to remain proactive in the management of your sales outlet. Analyzing sales data and working hours, then adjusting for peak periods, helps to better organize your teams. With a tool like IO Analytics, you canquickly identify areas of lost productivity and make the necessary adjustments.

5. Develop your team's skills

A well-trained team is a more efficient team! Make sure that every member is familiar with the tools used, service standards and new industry practices. Ongoing training not only helps to reduce errors, but also enhances the value of your team by reinforcing their sense of competence.

6. Promote effective communication and humane management

Fluid communication is essential for effective teamwork. Use messaging tools or organize regular briefings to keep everyone informed and ready to give their best. Management that valueslistening and caring helps maintain a good working atmosphere.

7. Improve order management

Good communication between the dining room and the kitchen is essential to improve the productivity of your teams. Optimize order dispatch to the kitchen with KDS (Kitchen Display System), which transmits orders from the cash register or kiosks directly to the kitchen team via a digital display. No more lost paper, errors or oversights.

"Thanks to KDS, everything runs smoothly during assembly, and assemblers don't make any mistakes." Albert, Alfi founder

👉 Read Alfi's testimonial

8. Simplify your menu to make serving easier

A complex menu can slow down service and stress kitchen teams. By opting for a simpler, more thoughtful menu, you can facilitate order-taking, reduce preparation time and improve workflow. A well-designed menu helps your team to stay efficient, even in the middle of a rush!

9. Adopt a recruitment strategy tailored to your needs

It's essential to recruit multi-skilled staff adapted to the demands of the fast-food industry. Anticipate peaks in activity and make sure youhave a team capable of meeting your customers' expectations, even at busy times. Well-thought-out recruitment allows you to be responsive andensure constant quality of service.

👉 Discover the webinar: How to boost productivity in fast food?

‍

Your team's driving force: well-being and motivation

  • Stimulate your team with bonuses and rewards: There's nothing like motivating objectives and rewards to boost your teams' commitment. Bonuses, monthly challenges or performance-based rewards: encourage every employee to give their best!
  • Promote well-being at work : well-being at work is a driver of productivity! Offer regular breaks, rest areas and encourage relaxing activities for a positive working environment. Numerous studies have shown that serene, well-rested teams are more productive, more stable and less prone to absenteeism.
  • Offer training and development opportunities: Develop a career plan by offering training and development opportunities. Because a team that feels valued is a team that is more committed to its work!

By following these tips, you'll have a clear and effective roadmap for improving your teams' productivity!
